value.rationale: The distinction between regional and joint occupancy under matched marginal catastrophes is naturally motivated, but the exact same all-parameter synchrony/rescue threshold and mean-occupancy phenomenon were published November 2, 2026. The only apparent addition, strict regional R decrease, is a one-line derivative of the earlier full p0 stationarity formula, not an independently useful exact unknown invariant, motivated new boundary, or nonroutine structural lemma. Reproducing the published algebra with a separate finite-state checker and renamed parameters has no surviving scientific contribution after subtracting the direct predecessor.

final_claim: For a two-patch symmetric binary occupancy CTMC with immigration lambda>0, ordinary local extinction mu>0, donor rescue c>0, fixed per-patch catastrophe hazard kappa>0 and common-shock sharing theta in [0,1], the stationary regional occupancy R and mean occupied count M strictly decrease with theta; stationary joint occupancy B increases, is constant, or decreases according as c is below, equal to, or above mu+kappa+lambda. Boundary synchronization optimizers are unique in strict cases, with the complete invariant distribution given in RESULT.md.
limitations: The current scientific claim is correct only for symmetric binary two-patch Poisson models with positive mainland immigration and fixed marginal hazard, stationary rather than finite-horizon persistence.
Public older ecological papers not all available in full; direct 2026-11-02 exact prior coverage is decisive regardless.
No broader patch networks, empirical hazard model, exact numerical error bounds or external certification established.
